qs.q:

Under the labour law, male and female workers must ______ equally for doing the same job.
qs.ex: Bị động với modal verb: must + be + V3/ed (be paid).

qs.q: Child marriage ought to ______ completely so that girls in rural areas can finish high school.
qs.ex: Bị động với ought to: ought to be + V3/ed (be stopped).

qs.q: Women should not ______ from applying for leadership positions in technology companies.
qs.ex: Bị động với should: should not be prevented.

qs.q: To become a qualified ______, a medical student must complete years of hospital training.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 6: surgeon = bác sĩ phẫu thuật.

qs.q: Domestic violence against women and children must ______ strictly by the law.
qs.ex: Bị động với must: must be punished.

qs.q: In the past, women were rarely allowed to train as fighter ______ in the air force.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 6: fighter pilots = phi công tiêm kích.

qs.q: More kindergarten teachers in our district are men, proving that childcare can ______ well by both genders.
qs.ex: Bị động với can: can be done.

qs.q: Equal educational opportunities should ______ to both boys and girls in mountainous communes.
qs.ex: Bị động với should: should be given.

qs.q: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman cosmonaut to fly into space with the Soviet ______ team.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 6 (bài nghe Valentina Tereshkova): parachutist = vận động viên nhảy dù.

qs.q: Outdated gender stereotypes may ______ if schools encourage girls to join robotics clubs.
qs.ex: Bị động với may: may be eliminated.

qs.q: Many women work in ______ jobs such as garment manufacturing and struggle to support their families.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 6: low-paying jobs = những công việc lương thấp.

qs.q: Household chores will ______ more fairly when both husband and wife work full time.
qs.ex: Bị động với will: will be shared.

qs.q: A firefighter must have great physical ______ and mental courage to rescue people from burning buildings.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 6: physical strength = thể lực, sức mạnh thể chất.

qs.q: Girls in every country should ______ to choose their own career path without family pressure.
qs.ex: Bị động với should: should be encouraged.

qs.q: Promoting gender ______ helps companies attract the best talent regardless of gender.

qs.q:
Mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best arrangement of utterances or sentences to make a cohesive and coherent exchange or text in each of the following questions from 7 to 11.
**Dear Alex,**
a. At school, our teachers also organise practical projects to help us allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
b. Thank you for your email; it was great to hear about your recent school activities.
c. At weekends, my friends and I join community groups to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace.
d. I’m writing to tell you about how we are learning about promoting gender equality in education and careers in Unit 6: Gender Equality.
e. Write back soon and tell me what your school is doing on this topic!
**Best wishes,**
qs.ex: Trình tự bức thư: Cảm ơn thư trước (b) → Nêu lý do viết thư chia sẻ chủ đề Unit (d) → Kể hoạt động ở trường (a) → Kể hoạt động cuối tuần (c) → Lời kết thư (e): b - d - a - c - e.

qs.q:
a. Nam: Yes, definitely! Let’s sign up together after class today.
b. Mai: Nam, our school club is holding a workshop on promoting gender equality in education and careers this Saturday. Would you like to join?
c. Mai: Great! I’ll get two registration forms from the club leader.
qs.ex: Trình tự hội thoại 3 lượt: Mai rủ Nam tham gia workshop chủ đề Unit (b) → Nam đồng ý đăng ký (a) → Mai nói sẽ đi lấy phiếu đăng ký (c): b - a - c.

qs.q:
a. To address this, schools and communities are now launching new career opportunities in the workplace.
b. In the past, many people did not pay enough attention to promoting gender equality in education and careers.
c. Today, however, both men and women realise how important it is to promote equal rights and fair pay.
d. As a result, everyone benefits when we work together to reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
e. These practical programmes help participants allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers in their daily lives.
qs.ex: Trình tự đoạn văn 5 câu: Thực trạng trước đây (b) → Nhận thức thay đổi ngày nay (c) → Giải pháp triển khai chương trình mới (a) → Tác dụng của các chương trình đó ('These practical programmes') (e) → Kết quả chung (d): b - c - a - e - d.

qs.q:
a. Linh: I’m preparing a poster about promoting gender equality in education and careers for our English lesson tomorrow.
b. Minh: That sounds interesting! What main benefit are you highlighting on the poster?
c. Minh: Well done, Linh. I’m sure our classmates will learn a lot from your presentation!
d. Linh: I’m focusing on how career opportunities can allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers and reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
e. Minh: What are you working on, Linh? You look really focused.
qs.ex: Trình tự hội thoại 5 lượt: Minh hỏi Linh đang làm gì (e) → Linh nói đang làm poster cho bài học tiếng Anh (a) → Minh hỏi lợi ích chính trên poster là gì (b) → Linh giải thích nội dung (d) → Minh khen ngợi (c): e - a - b - d - c.

qs.q:
a. Next, participants work in small groups to discuss practical ways to promote equal rights and fair pay.
b. After the opening talk, the organisers show a short video on how career opportunities work in the workplace.
c. Every month, our youth club organises a special morning session dedicated to promoting gender equality in education and careers.
d. By noon, everyone leaves with useful tips to allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers every day.
e. First, an experienced speaker welcomes the men and women and introduces the main topic.
qs.ex: Trình tự đoạn văn theo thời gian: Giới thiệu buổi sinh hoạt hàng tháng (c) → Đầu tiên diễn giả chào mừng (e) → Sau bài phát biểu mở đầu là xem video (b) → Tiếp theo thảo luận nhóm (a) → Đến trưa mọi người ra về với kiến thức bổ ích (d): c - e - b - a - d.

**UNDERSTANDING UNIT 6: GENDER EQUALITY**
Across many communities today, career opportunities are becoming an essential part of modern life. Activities **(12)**______ by local schools and organisations help men and women understand the value of promoting gender equality in education and careers.
At present, more young people **(13)**______ practical ways to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace. **(14)**______ starting a new habit takes effort, the long-term benefits are undeniable. People who actively take part in these initiatives **(15)**______ more confident and better prepared for the future.
**(16)**______ through a small daily action or a weekend community project, everyone can help allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
(Adapted from Global Success – Unit 6: Gender Equality)
qs.ex: Rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ bị động ('Activities which are organised by...'): organised.

**COMMUNITY ACTION AND PEER MENTORING IN UNIT 6: GENDER EQUALITY**
Last year, youth unions in three provinces launched a six-month pilot programme to promote promoting gender equality in education and careers at the grassroots level. Instead of relying on formal lectures, organisers trained two hundred high school volunteers to lead weekend activities where neighbours could promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace. Within the first two months, local communities reported <u>**tangible**</u> improvements in daily habits and neighbourhood solidarity.
A key factor behind this success was peer-to-peer mentoring. Teenagers often feel intimidated when adults lecture them, but they respond enthusiastically when classmates demonstrate how career opportunities can allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers. By working in small teams of five or six, participants shared practical tips, solved everyday problems together and helped one another reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
Organisers also introduced simple tools to keep momentum high. **[I]** Every participating household received a visual progress board to track weekly milestones. **[II]** Local cultural centres hosted monthly gatherings where teams showcased their most creative ideas. **[III]** These celebrations turned routine tasks into a source of shared pride across the entire district. **[IV]**
Follow-up surveys conducted six months later confirmed that over seventy-five per cent of participants continued practising career opportunities independently. When student volunteers take ownership of community initiatives, <u>**their**</u> enthusiasm inspires both younger children and older residents. The pilot programme demonstrates that youth-led action is one of the most powerful ways to bring the values of Unit 6: Gender Equality to life.
(Adapted from Community Development & Youth Studies – Unit 6: Gender Equality)

**THE RIPPLE EFFECT OF PEER LEADERSHIP IN UNIT 6: GENDER EQUALITY**
How do positive habits spread across a school or neighbourhood? Sociologists studying promoting gender equality in education and careers have discovered that peer influence is often stronger than formal rules. When men and women see their close friends willingly engage in career opportunities, they are far more likely to join in and allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
Nevertheless, launching a new initiative is never without challenges. Organisers note that initial doubts and busy routines are common, and <u>**they**</u> can slow down participation during the first week. <u>**Young people learn most effectively when they observe respected peers applying positive habits in real-life situations.**</u>
For this reason, many schools encourage <u>**voluntary**</u> student ambassadors to lead by example. Whether demonstrating how to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace or sharing practical tips during break time, these role models create a welcoming ripple effect that helps the whole school reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
Even when a minor <u>**obstacle**</u> arises, a supportive peer group keeps members motivated. What begins as the effort of a few enthusiastic students soon grows into a proud tradition shared by the entire community.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 6: Gender Equality)

Mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best arrangement of utterances or sentences to make a meaningful exchange or text in each of the following questions from 7 to 11.
**Dear Kenji,**
a. Outside the classroom, we also take part in practical activities to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace.
b. How do students in Japan learn about this topic? Write back soon and tell me!
c. This month in Viet Nam, high school students are studying Unit 6: Gender Equality, which focuses on promoting gender equality in education and careers.
d. These experiences have taught my classmates and me how to allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers and reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
e. Thank you for your postcard from Tokyo; I loved reading about your school festival.
**Best wishes,**
qs.ex: Trình tự thư gửi bạn qua thư Kenji: e (cảm ơn bưu thiếp từ Tokyo) → c (giới thiệu bài học tháng này tại Việt Nam) → a (hoạt động thực tế ngoài lớp học) → d (bài học rút ra) → b (câu hỏi kết thư).

qs.q:
a. Ngọc: That’s wonderful news! All our hard work researching career opportunities really paid off.
b. Đức: She praised our practical examples of how men and women can allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
c. Đức: Ngọc, our English teacher just returned our group report on Unit 6: Gender Equality with an A+!
qs.ex: Trình tự hội thoại 3 lượt: c (Đức báo tin bài báo cáo nhóm đạt A+) → b (Đức kể lời nhận xét của cô giáo) → a (Ngọc bày tỏ niềm vui).

qs.q:
a. Positive role models play a crucial part in spreading the values of Unit 6: Gender Equality.
b. Gradually, this peer-to-peer encouragement builds a culture where everyone wants to reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
c. Inspired by their example, younger students become much more willing to allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
d. When respected student leaders actively practise career opportunities, their classmates quickly take notice.
e. Therefore, schools should empower youth ambassadors to lead initiatives on promoting gender equality in education and careers.
qs.ex: Trình tự đoạn văn: a (câu chủ đề về vai trò của tấm gương tích cực) → d (khi các thủ lĩnh học sinh làm gương) → c (Inspired by their example...) → b (Gradually...) → e (Therefore: kết luận).

qs.q:
a. Vy: Hoàng, now that our month-long project on Unit 6: Gender Equality is finished, what impressed you the most?
b. Hoàng: Definitely! And what about you, Vy?
c. Hoàng: I was amazed by how enthusiastically men and women worked together to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace.
d. Vy: I learned that consistent career opportunities can truly allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers and reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society.
e. Vy: I agree! Seeing everyone cooperate so closely was unforgettable.

**EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND THE FUTURE OF UNIT 6: GENDER EQUALITY**
Across Viet Nam, forward-thinking high schools are transforming how students learn about promoting gender equality in education and careers. Rather than treating Unit 6: Gender Equality as a set of vocabulary items to memorise for a test, teachers are integrating experiential learning into every week of the semester. Educators agree that hands-on practice is <u>**indispensable**</u> if young people are to allow both men and women to pursue their dream careers.
In these classrooms, students work in project teams to investigate real issues and propose ways to promote equal rights and fair pay in the workplace. For instance, learners might interview local residents, design bilingual awareness posters or organise a school-wide campaign on career opportunities. Through these authentic tasks, men and women discover how their classroom English connects directly to everyday life.
Assessment methods are evolving alongside teaching styles. **[I]** Instead of relying solely on written quizzes, schools evaluate how effectively students collaborate and apply their plans. **[II]** Each team keeps a reflective portfolio documenting the challenges they faced and how their actions helped reduce poverty and boost economic growth for the whole society. **[III]** This approach rewards creativity, persistence and genuine teamwork rather than rote memorisation. **[IV]**
Graduates of experiential programmes consistently report higher confidence when entering university and the workplace. Students <u>**who**</u> have practised solving real-world problems in high school adapt much faster to new environments. By making promoting gender equality in education and careers an active, lived experience, education equips the next generation with both language proficiency and civic responsibility.
(Adapted from Modern Curriculum & Pedagogy Journal – Unit 6: Gender Equality)
